correctness.rationale: Edge vanishing on a segment of a polynomial extends to the supporting line. After scaling the cube to [-1,1]^3, sign-flip averaging decomposes each candidate harmonic polynomial into eight parity sectors x^epsilon1 y^epsilon2 z^epsilon3 Q_epsilon(u,v,w), where u=x²-1 etc. Vanishing on every supporting coordinate line is exactly Q_epsilon in J=(uv,uw,vw). The degree<=6 bound restricts each Q degree: triple-odd sector vanishes by degree, six non-even sectors have only uv,uw,vw and an invertible 3x3 Laplacian coefficient matrix with determinant -2(2+4e1)(2+4e2)(2+4e3). The even sector has ten monomials in J of degree<=3; transformed Laplacian has a 9x10 coefficient matrix with a nonzero 9x9 minor 110592, so its kernel is at most one-dimensional. I independently used exact SymPy algebra to confirm this minor, rank 9, all parity determinants and harmonicity and twelve edge-line restrictions of V=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w). Therefore the kernel is span{(x²-y²)(x²-z²)(y²-z²)}; degree-six existence and nonexistence below six follow for all real/complex nonhomogeneous polynomials, not by sampling isolated edges.
